sections.title: The letter pi
paragraphs: The letter (pi) /pi/ makes the sound of the letter itself. Its main sound is heard in (pane) /ˈpa.ne/, which means bread. This letter makes two sounds, short and long.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Close both lips firmly to stop the airflow completely. Release the air suddenly without breathing out extra air. For the longer sound, hold your lips closed twice as long before opening them. Keep your vocal cords silent while your lips are closed. Put your hand on your throat to feel no vibration.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In most places, this letter makes the sound /p/, that is a short p, as in (aperto) /aˈpɛr.to/. When written double or between two connected words, it makes the sound /pː/, that is a long double p, as in (cappa) /ˈkap.pa/.

sections.title: Tips for English speakers
paragraphs: You might release a small puff of breath, like in the English word pet. Hold your breath back completely, like after the s in spin. Hold a paper before your mouth to see it stay still.
